# Zone control and escaping

## In short
- A zone in the World Beyond is **under control** while the control points (CP) of the living citizens in it add up to at least the number of zombies there. If the zombies outnumber your CP, you can't move, dig or enter an explorable ruin.
- Each citizen gives 2 CP. A Riot Shield, a `defence_cp` item, the Guide role and some hero skills add more. Terror sets your CP to 0.
- If you are trapped, you have these ways out:
  - a desperate escape, which costs a wound and gives you 5 minutes to move;
  - an escape item: Grisly Bomb 40 s, Pre-war camera 120 s, Flash Grenade 300 s;
  - a scout's Camouflage Vest, which lets you walk through uncontrolled zones but can be spotted.
- When someone leaves a zone and the zombies take over, the citizens left behind get a 30-minute grace timer to leave.

## How it works

### Control points and control
- **When a zone is controlled.** The zone is under control if the summed CP of the alive citizens in it is ≥ the number of zombies [1]. Action requirements use the same test (`isControlled`: CP ≥ zombies) [2].
- **A citizen's CP.** If the citizen has the `terror` status, their CP is 0. Otherwise it is the sum of [3]:
  - base 2;
  - plus the citizen property ZoneControlBonus (0 by default) [4];
  - +2 if they carry an unbroken Riot Shield (`shield_#00`);
  - +1 if they carry an unbroken item with the `defence_cp` property;
  - for the `guide` role: + the number of citizens in the zone, counting the guide;
  - + ZoneControlCleanBonus if they have the `clean` status;
  - + ZoneControlHydratedBonus if they have neither `thirst1` nor `thirst2`. This also sets the `hydrated` status, which is removed when the condition fails;
  - + ZoneControlSoberBonus if they are neither `drunk` nor `hungover`. This also sets or removes the `sober` status.
  
  The three status bonuses (clean, hydrated, sober) are 0 by default [4].

### What a blocked (uncontrolled) zone prevents
- **Moving.** You can't move unless you have an active escape timer (desperate timers count) or wear `vest_on_#00` [5].
  - When you lead escorts, every mover is checked on their own. The whole move fails if any one of them is blocked [5].
- **Digging.** You can't start digging [5]. During a zone update, if CP < zombies, every dig timer becomes passive and nothing is found [6].
- **Explorable ruins.** You can't enter one unless you wear `vest_on_#00` [5].
- **Bare-hand attack** (1 AP, 8% chance to kill a zombie, 4% when drunk). Unusually, this is only *possible* in an uncontrolled zone. It is refused if:
  - you have any active escape timer, including a desperate one;
  - you wear the vest;
  - you have `terror` or a hand wound (`wound2`) [5].

### Losing control: the grace timer
- The check runs whenever citizens leave a zone. If the zone was controlled before and is no longer, while citizens remain, the game:
  - logs "control lost" naming the citizen who left;
  - adds a zone escape timer of **+30 minutes**;
  - makes every dig timer in the zone passive, logging "search interrupted" [1].
- If control comes back, the game logs "zone under control" [1].
- If the zone becomes empty, all its escape timers and smoke-bomb timers are deleted [1].
- On each zone update, expired escape timers are removed. If no valid timer is left, the zone is still uncontrolled and citizens are present, an "escape timer expired" entry is logged [7].

### Desperate escape
- **Conditions.** You must be able to act, and all of these must hold [5]:
  - the zone is not controlled;
  - no escape timer is running (desperate ones included);
  - you don't wear `vest_on_#00`;
  - you don't have `terror`;
  - you are not already wounded.
  
  The dashboard also greys the button out when you are tired [8].
- **Effect.**
  - You receive one random wound (head, hand, arms, leg, eye or foot), and it is logged.
  - You get a personal **desperate** escape timer of **5 minutes** [5].
- **What the timer allows.** It lets you move [5]. The camouflage checks do *not* count desperate timers (they call `getEscapeTimeout` without allowing them) [5] [3].

### Escape items
- **What they do.** An item effect with `escape` > 0 adds an escape timer of `escape` seconds to every zone within `escapeRange`. These timers are attached to the zone, with no citizen. The use is logged in your zone [9].
- **Inside an explorable ruin room,** the escape effect instead removes all the room's zombies and spreads them elsewhere in the ruin [10].
- **The items:**
  - **Flash Grenade (`flash_#00`):** 300 s in your zone. Usable outside or while exploring, only when blocked ("must_be_blocked") [11].
  - **Grisly Bomb (`flesh_#00`):** 40 s, only when blocked [12].
  - **Pre-war camera (`photo_4_#00`):** 120 s, only when blocked and with zombies present. It then becomes `photo_3_#00`. At a ruin whose blueprint is still available, a separate variant also gives the blueprint [13].
  - **Catapult:** a Flash Grenade or Grisly Bomb fired by the catapult gives a 300 s escape timer to the target zone and the zones within 1 [11] [12].

### Moving and timers
- **Your own timers.** Moving deletes all your own escape timers and makes your dig timer passive [5].
- **Timers in the zone you reach.** If the destination zone is under control after the move, all its escape timers are deleted [5].
- **The zone you leave.** The 30-minute grace logic above runs for that zone [5].
- **Move cost.** 1 AP. When the zone is 3 km or more from town, your other point pool (SP) is used first and AP is the fallback [5].
- **Interrupted moves.** With a leg wound (`wound4`), a move fails 20% of the time. With `terror` in a zone that has zombies, it fails 5% of the time. Either way you lose 1 point and stay put [5].

### Camouflage (scout's Camouflage Vest)
- **Putting it on.** `vest_off_#00` → `vest_on_#00`.
  - In the World Beyond, this needs no followers and a controlled or temporarily controlled zone.
  - In town it has no condition [14].
- **While worn,** the vest:
  - lets you move out of uncontrolled zones and enter explorable ruins in them;
  - blocks desperate escape and bare-hand attack [5].
- **Spotting when entering a zone.** This applies only to the scout job (`hunter`) wearing the vest. The check runs when the destination zone's CP is below its zombies. That CP is the CP already in the zone plus the CP of everyone moving [5].
  1. delta = floor((zombies − CP) × 1.3)
  2. At night: delta − 5. This uses the night clock even if the town's night mode is switched off.
  3. If delta ≤ 6, delta is halved.
  4. Chance of losing the vest = max(0, delta − 3 × zone scout level) / 100.
  
  For example, 10 zombies against 2 CP, by day, at scout level 0, gives delta 10 and a 10% chance [5].
  
  After the check, the scout leaves a ScoutVisit marker on the zone [5].
- **Losing the vest by acting.** In an uncontrolled zone with no (non-desperate) escape timer, these actions take the vest off for certain:
  - item actions that don't "keep cover", including escort actions;
  - heroic actions that don't "keep cover" [5];
  - searching a building [15];
  - clearing debris [16];
  - moving items [17].
  
  Losing it turns `vest_on_#00` into `vest_off_#00` [3].

### Escorts
- **Who can lead.** The leader must be a hero or have the `guide` role, must not be banished, and must not be in learning mode. They can lead at most `features.escort.max` followers (4 by default). The citizen being escorted must have switched escort on [5] [18].
- **Moving as a group.**
  - Escorted citizens can't move on their own [5].
  - Escorts move with the leader. Each one is checked separately for blocking, points and over-encumbrance.
  - A follower's leg wound or terror cancels the whole move. The follower who failed loses 1 point.
  - A follower set to "force direct return" refuses moves away from town. When they reach the town zone they enter automatically if the door is open, unless the Labyrinth is built [5].
  - Followers' CP counts toward the destination zone's CP in the scout spotting check [5].
  - Someone who moves alone loses their escort settings [5].
- **Restrictions while leading.** You can't enter an explorable ruin while leading escorts [5], and you can't put the vest on [14].
- **Digging.** The leader can start digs for all followers or for one of them, but only in a controlled zone [5].

## What changes it
- **Riot Shield (`shield_#00`):** +2 CP if unbroken. Strapping it on your back turns it into `shield_off_#00`, which no longer counts [3] [19].
- **Car Door (`car_door_#00`):** the only item with the `defence_cp` property: +1 CP if unbroken. Carrying several gives no more.
- **`defence_cp` items:** +1 CP if you carry at least one unbroken item with this property [3].
- **Guide role:** + the number of citizens in the zone. It also lets the citizen lead escorts [3] [5].
- **Hero skill Healthy Body** (61 hero days, legacy skill): +1 CP while you stay `clean` (`props.bonus.zone_control.clean` = 1) [20].
- **Statuses:**
  - `terror` → 0 CP, blocks desperate escape, and gives a 5% chance a move fails in a zone with zombies;
  - `wound4` → 20% chance a move fails;
  - any wound blocks desperate escape;
  - `drunk` halves the bare-hand attack chance [3] [5].
- **Scout job (`hunter`):** the only job checked for vest spotting [5].
- **Upgraded map (`item_electro_#00`):** shows exact zombie counts in zones you enter [5].

## Town types
- **Rule files.** The default, small, remote, panda and custom rule files that I read set no zone-control or escape setting. Their differences are elsewhere: map size, camping, oxygen and so on [21] [22] [23] [24].
- **Escorts.** The default settings are `features.escort.enabled` = true and `max` = 4. None of the town-type diffs I read change them [18].
- **Night mode in small towns.** Small towns switch night mode off. The scout spotting −5 at night still applies there, because it ignores that setting [21] [5].

## Related
- Scouts, scout levels and ScoutVisit markers [25].
- Explorable ruins: inside a ruin, fleeing costs 15–24 s of oxygen [26].
- Digging [6].
- Heroic return and rescue, which dissolve escorts and update zone control [27].
- Weapons that kill zombies [10].

## Not verified
- **Zone-wide timers.** I could not read the escape-timer lookup code (`EscapeTimerRepository::findActiveByCitizen`). So it is unconfirmed that zone timers with no citizen attached apply to everyone in the zone. These are the 30-minute grace timer and the timers from escape items.
- **"Blocked" in item requirements.** I could not find the exact condition behind `must_be_blocked` / `must_be_blocked_hd`. It is probably "not controlled and not temporarily controlled".
- **Whether the Guardian starts with the Riot Shield.**
- **Other CP sources.** I found no source in the documents for ZoneControlBonus, ZoneControlHydratedBonus or ZoneControlSoberBonus besides the default of 0.
- **Heroic punch.** Its escape time (property HeroPunchEscapeTime, default 0; HeroPunchKills, default 2) exists, but I did not trace its effect.
